## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no results yet. In earlier searches, recipe changes never moved a zero. The one success came from hedging how the mask maps onto the action layout. So round 1 tests which assumption this world breaks. All six candidates use the reference trunk and recipe, and each changes one assumption: (1) the reference unchanged, as the control; (2) 16 action layouts (8 grid symmetries × type-major/minor order) on both the mask input and the output maps; (3) a 5x5 head conv, hedging footprint size and anchor offset; (4) DONE as the first action as well as the last; (5) the obs flipped or transposed relative to the mask; (6) all of these combined. Obs channel order needs no separate bet because the learned 1x1 stem treats all channels alike. All files fall back to Linear mask embeddings if n_place ≠ T·Y·X. With one seed, gaps under about 0.07 may be noise, and any nonzero training success is the signal to follow.

### Round 2
All six round-1 trials scored 0, both on dev and in training. Parameter counts match T=4, in_channels=27 and n_place=T*Y*X, so the spec sizes hold. If the world is learnable, round 1 makes several deviations unlikely: action layouts within the 8 grid symmetries times type order, DONE at index 0, anchor shifts of up to 2 cells or larger footprints, and the obs flipped or transposed relative to the mask. The kitchen-sink net combined all of these and still scored 0. So the deviation is probably not a layout problem. It may stop learning itself: an odd obs scale, a large reward or value scale whose gradients swamp the shared trunk, or a near-random policy at start once many hedged maps are summed. Or the dynamics may need wider spatial reasoning. This round, each candidate bets on one such learning bottleneck on top of the reference net. One candidate combines them all with the 16-layout hedge, and one adds a recipe aimed at exploration.

### Round 3
All 12 trials score 0 on dev and in training. The parameter counts confirm the spec: the reference's 53,130 params match in_channels=27 (Z=6), n_types=4 and n_place=4·Y·X+1 exactly. So the action count and grid size are as described, and the mask-reshape path is valid. These deviations are ruled out or unhelpful:
- the 16 symmetry/type-order layouts of the mask and actions;
- DONE at index 0;
- whole-obs y/x flips and transpose;
- 5x5 anchor hedges;
- GroupNorm, near-uniform init, separate critic, global context and footprint pooling;
- a 1-epoch exploration recipe.

A learned 1x1 stem already undoes any permutation of obs channels. Local dynamics changes (no drop, other heights) are learnable by these convnets. What remains structurally unlearnable is a spatial scramble of the obs memory that no grid symmetry undoes, for example a channels-last (Y,X,C) buffer read as (C,Y,X), or an arbitrary fixed action permutation. This round bets on those, using explicit reinterpretations and learned dense remaps that start at full scale.

### Round 4
All 18 trials scored 0 on dev and in training. The parameter counts confirm the spec as described (T=4, Y=X=8, Z=6, n_place=256), so the layout hedges were active in every trial. The results rule out several deviations, assuming the net could otherwise learn: the action layout under all 16 symmetry and type-order variants; DONE at index 0; the obs flipped, rotated or channels-last; any fixed scramble a dense remap can learn quickly; obs channel permutations, since the 1x1 stem absorbs them; footprint or anchor shifts up to 2 cells; and obs scale, critic interference and starting-policy collapse. That leaves deviations in dynamics or reward, non-local frame offsets, or a world too hard for this budget. This is the last round, so I spread the bets. Two trials use the most samples possible (1 PPO epoch, about 430k steps); one stretches the horizon for a sparse-bonus world. One adds non-local self-attention, one a z-factored per-layer encoder for vertical dynamics, and one combines everything with maximum samples.
